_comment: Permission policy for edullm-dataset-publish -- the GENERAL-PURPOSE publisher role. Any dataset,
any family, one role. Supersedes the pattern of a new role per corpus.
WHY GENERAL RATHER THAN PER-CORPUS. `edullm-prm800k-producer` hardcodes
`vendor/openai-prm800k/*` in five of its six statements, so it can publish exactly one dataset
and a second corpus needed a second role (09-reservoir-publish-*.json, now superseded by this).
That does not scale, and worse, it makes the per-corpus role the path of least resistance --
each one a fresh chance to fat-finger a Deny. One reviewed role that every publish job assumes
is both less work and less surface.
WHAT BOUNDS IT INSTEAD OF A DATASET NAME: the Section 2 family enum. `contracts.validate_dataset_id`
refuses any dataset_id whose first segment is not one of the seven families below (verified:
`_ingest/evil` and `_dist/evil` both raise NamingError), so scoping the grant to those seven
prefixes means this role cannot write to the pipeline's own control prefixes -- `_ingest/`
(build staging), `_dist/` (bootstrap wheels, NO lifecycle expiry so a poisoned wheel would sit
there indefinitely), or `_catalog/`. A wildcard on `edullm-landing/*` would have granted all
three, and nothing in publish() needs them.
THE AIRLOCK IS UNTOUCHED. All writes here are to edullm-landing. edullm-data is writable ONLY
by the validator role, enforced by a Deny in 02-bucket-policy.json, and re-Denied here so that
attaching a broad managed policy to this role later cannot quietly open it. publish() stages;
promote() -- the validator's job -- is what crosses the airlock.
WHY IT MAY WRITE manifest.json AND dataset.json, which the BUILD roles are explicitly denied.
Those two names fire `edullm-landing-manifest-created` and reserve a version, and a builder that
could write them could fire the validator against a half-built prefix. Publishing is precisely
the step that is supposed to write them, so the Deny cannot apply here -- which is why this is a
separate identity from `edullm-reservoir-ingest` rather than a widening of it.
STILL DENIED: the validator's terminal markers. A producer that could write `_VALIDATED.json`
could make a REJECTED upload look promoted, which is the one forgery that would silently defeat
the whole gate. Denied bucket-wide, not per-dataset.
READS on edullm-data are needed because publish() resolves the next version from the published
catalog and binds a published tokenizer by reading its tokenizer.json. Read-only, and narrowed
to the two prefixes that serve those purposes.
